name: Audity DJ
author: Audity
description: The talking DJ for the Audity app, on Navidrome, Jellyfin or Plex: Theo's lines from a bank of clips made ahead, with only the names said on this server, only while a DJ session is on, and what the DJ remembers for each account, shared by all your devices.

versions.changelog: Ask the DJ for a song by its exact title, an album or an artist, as you'd say it, and it finds it. Ask it to add something to your queue, or to play it next, and it does, with the song on playing on. Asking it to change the vibe changes it from the next song. It understands what you mean, not only names: songs for a rainy day, something you haven't heard in a while, an artist's newest album, more like the song on or the rest of its album, and who's singing. Only the DJ's small program comes down again (57 KB); the voice and the bank stay as they are. Audity's next update uses all of it.

The DJ itself is now a small program of its own, which the plugin downloads the first time it starts (45 KB) and runs beside AudioMuse-AI, on this server only. There's nothing to do: the voice, the bank, the artists' facts and everything the DJ remembers stay as they are, nothing else is downloaded again, and Audity works as before. Everything works with the server's internet down: a Plex sign-in no longer asks plex.tv each time, once a device has signed in while it was up. The voices from before Theo's bank, and their code, are gone.

Ready for the DJ to remember: your server keeps every song the DJ plays for you, on any device, and whether you skipped it, and every set it played, for good, so Audity can rest songs by time and say when it last played you one. Audity can also ask how long each line lasts, so the DJ can finish talking before the singing starts. Nothing to download again, and nothing changes until Audity's next update uses it.

Years you ask for are the years that are read: "80s not 90s", "No, 80s" and "give me some 80s music" ask for the eighties, also where a song, album or artist in your library is called something like Give Me Some. Such a name still plays when you ask for it by name. Nothing to download again.

On a first install, the DJ talks as soon as Theo's bank is in, while the artists' facts are still coming down, and stopping the download there, or AudioMuse-AI restarting, keeps the bank: in 1.8.5 it waited for the facts, and the next try downloaded the bank again. Audity can now see when an update is ready and its size, for the same one Update the Voice the plugin's page shows. Nothing to download again.

Ready for the DJ to tell you about the music: Update the Voice brings the artists' facts from MusicBrainz (173 MB, free to use), who's a person or a band, when they were born or formed, where they're from and their albums in order, looked up on your server, so nothing about your library is sent anywhere. Audity can also ask each song's pace, key, energy and moods from AudioMuse-AI's own analysis, which needs no download. Whatever is new comes as one Update the Voice, its size said once; the bank you have stays. Nothing is said differently yet: the lines that use the facts come with release 2's bank.

What you ask for is read, whatever kind it is: decades and years however they're said or written ("’80s", "eighties", "early 90s", "1975 to 1983"), genres however they're spelled, artists, albums and songs by name, moods, and the app's own suggestions, each said back as you said it. A name, a year or a genre that isn't in your library is said to be missing, where before AudioMuse-AI's sound search played something else. The newest request replaces the one before unless it says to build on it. Nothing to download again. For release 2's bigger bank, ready ahead: the server can keep which sentences each account has heard; the bank's sentences are sent to Audity compressed; and a bank past 2 GB comes down in parts.

When AudioMuse-AI can't reach your Navidrome, Jellyfin or Plex at the address it has saved (the server moved to another machine, say), the app is told so, with the one step to fix it: update that address in AudioMuse-AI's settings. Before, it was told its sign-in was turned down. Nothing to download again.

Theo's bank is the only voice: the plugin's page no longer lists the voices from before it (Theo and Juno, and voices added by hand) or adding a voice, and Try a Line says it in the bank, as nothing says a line in them now. NeuTTS Air and Ming, the voices before the bank, are removed once the bank is in if they're still on the server (3.4 and 4.5 GB). Nothing to download again.

Theo's bank made again with his voice trained once more, so his moods come through more: about 10,600 sentences, as loud as 1.7.0's. Tap Download the New Bank on the plugin's page (0.33 GB); the bank before keeps talking until it's in, and is then removed.

Asking the DJ, understood on this server: for the Audity builds that send what you said, your words are read here against your own library (play something, starting with a song, no more or less of something, more like this, something different, older or newer, your most played, new releases, deep cuts, throwbacks), with no language model, and a feel that names nothing ("something chill for a rainy night") goes to AudioMuse-AI's own text search where CLAP is on. The next songs' names are said ahead, so the DJ's lines come back at once. The same bank as 1.7.0, so nothing to download again.

Theo louder: his bank made again about 6 dB louder, so he isn't quiet against the music, with the names said as loud. About 10,600 sentences now, with lines remade that came out wrong before and new ways to say your play counts. Tap Download the New Bank on the plugin's page (0.32 GB); the bank before keeps talking until it's in, and is then removed.

Theo's new bank: about 9,700 sentences made ahead by Qwen3-TTS, with many more ways to say each kind of line, and the names said on this server by Pocket TTS in the same voice, in under a second. Tap Download the New Bank on the plugin's page (0.29 GB); the bank before keeps talking until it's in, and is then removed. Audity picks up the new sentences on its own.

Back to Theo's bank, as in 1.4.2: 1.5.0's whole lines were too slow on a NAS, and a song change could go by with no line. The DJ talks from the bank's clips again, with only the names said on this server. Nothing to download again.
Whole lines, said in one go by Pocket TTS in a new voice for Theo and written on this server from what's playing. Taken out in 1.5.1.

Each sentence of the DJ's lines ends whole: a soft last word ("library", "evening") was cut off slightly where the pieces of a line were joined, and now fades out as it was recorded. Lines kept from before are made again the new way.

The DJ's voice stays loaded once it's downloaded, so it's ready the moment you start the DJ, even after the app was closed, and it starts again on its own should it ever stop. A line the app needs right away (the DJ button's, a skip's) is made before the lines for songs further ahead, and a closed session's waiting lines are let go. The page lists the last lines asked and how each was made. Names are said a little quicker, on Pocket TTS's own single thread. For the app: the bank's sentences at /app/bank.

The DJ talks from Theo's bank: about 5,900 sentences made ahead, played as clips, so most lines are ready at once. Only the names of songs, artists and albums are said on this server, by Pocket TTS (Kyutai, CC-BY-4.0) in Theo's voice, in about a second; a line never waits more than a few seconds for them. Tap Download the Voice once (about 1.5 GB). Your earlier voice talks until it's in, and can be removed after. While the bank is the voice, the DJ is Theo.

The plugin's page works again: in 1.3.0 a mistake in its script left it showing … with no way to download the voice. The page also fills in at once, not after several seconds, and no longer keeps the server busy while it's open.

A new voice, NeuTTS Air (Neuphonic, Apache-2.0), about three times quicker on a processor, so a line is ready well before its song: tap Download the Voice again (3.4 GB). Theo is a new, deeper and cleaner voice. Your earlier voice stays until the new one is in, and can be removed after. A colon in a line now gets a full stop's pause, so a name after it no longer runs on. A take the voice says nothing in is made again, not the line lost.
Lines made faster again: the voice's language model no longer works out word guesses it never uses, about half its work a step, with the sound exactly the same.
Lines made about twice as fast in the voice's flow head, its weights in 8 bits, with the sound kept (the language model, which sets the words and their timing, stays in full precision).
Try a Line says it in the voice picked, those added for one account too, and shows where the time went on this server: loading the voice, speaking, and checking.
A cleaner page in AudioMuse-AI's own style: each voice's name, description and account can be edited, as Audity shows them, and its clip played from its row.
Lines at the voice's full quality (44.1 kHz) for the Audity builds that play it; earlier builds still get 24 kHz.

Jellyfin and Plex accounts sign in too; the voices are named Theo and Juno; lines said before are kept and sent at once; a line is sent the moment it's made; songs that sound alike for the server you signed in to; the crackle between pauses fixed; the page's downloads and voices kept to AudioMuse-AI's admins.
First release: the DJ's voice (Ming-3.0-tts 0.5B on the processor), two voices and your own, lines checked with speech-to-text, and the DJ's memory per Navidrome account.
